lines: Drum trigger sequencer: up to 25 named phrases of drum notes across ten voices, with per-note velocity, accents, ratchets, flams and probability, edited in a popup piano roll
The clock that drives playback, at four ticks per beat, which a clock module calls x4 or 1/16th
Chooses which of the 25 phrases plays, C3 selecting the first and the 25 semitones up to C5 the last; set to trigger on the menu it steps to the next non-empty phrase or picks one at random
A trigger returning the playhead to the beginning, or to the start repeat marker with that option set on the menu; playback carries on immediately if the sequencer is running
A trigger toggling between running and stopped; while stopped the gates are closed and clock ticks are ignored
Returns the playhead to the beginning, or to the start repeat marker with that option set on the menu
Starts and stops playback
Starts and stops recording of the notes arriving at the record inputs into the current phrase
Clears every note out of the current phrase
Records drum notes from a keyboard, the ten white keys from C4 to E5 playing the ten voices
Records drum notes from a General MIDI drum kit, whose standard kit notes are mapped onto the ten voices
The note-on trigger for recording, taken from the gate output of a MIDI-CV module
Sets the velocity of each recorded note
A trigger on each note played by that voice
A trigger on each note of that voice that is marked as an accent in the editor
The velocity of the note being played by that voice
A trigger each time the playhead reaches the end of the phrase
Note — the large display draws the phrase with the playhead as a vertical line, and clicking it opens an editor for adding, moving and deleting notes and setting velocity, accent and probability
Note — the small display names the phrase now playing, and clicking it lists the 25 phrases to choose from
Note — a MIDI file can be imported from the editor or dragged onto it from disk, and the sequence exported to a MIDI file from there
Note — a swing pattern set in the editor offsets quarter, eighth or sixteenth notes forwards or backwards by a chosen fraction, and a pattern set on a narrower part overrides a broader one
Note — with Record enabled and Run switched off, each note played at the record inputs is written at the playhead, which then steps on by the quantisation amount
Menu — Phrase selection input reads the phrase input as a pitch from C3 to C5, as a trigger stepping to the next non-empty phrase, or as a trigger picking a random phrase
Menu — Shared playhead links this module to other Entrian sequencers, one marked leader and the rest followers, so that all their playheads move together
Menu — Delay Clock/Reset/Run inputs adds a delay of a whole number of samples to those three inputs, to make up for the one-sample delay every cable in Rack adds; Auto is the default
Menu — Set playhead to start marker on reset sends a reset to the start repeat marker instead of to the beginning
Menu — Stop recording at end of song ends recording when the playhead reaches the end, without a second press of Record
Menu — Automatically add repeat markers when recording drops a start marker where recording began and an end marker where it stopped, and the playhead then loops that section
Menu — Light theme and Dark theme choose the panel colours
Menu — Save patch to use the free Entrian Player writes a copy of the patch with every Entrian sequencer replaced by its play-only counterpart from the Entrian Free plugin
Drummer.notes: The panel prints C4-E5 on the voice record input; Entrian's Acoustic Drums page calls it C4-D5, and the panel is followed here because ten white keys starting at C4 end on E5. The Reset and Run output jacks are not described in the manual, on the panel or in the binary, so they are left untagged.

lines: Control voltage sequencer: up to 25 named phrases of drawn CV segments across 16 channels, played out as a polyphonic voltage with gate and velocity
The clock that drives playback, at four ticks per beat, which a clock module calls x4 or 1/16th
Chooses which of the 25 phrases plays, C3 selecting the first and the 25 semitones up to C5 the last; set to trigger on the menu it steps to the next non-empty phrase or picks one at random
A trigger returning the playhead to the beginning, or to the start repeat marker with that option set on the menu; playback carries on immediately if the sequencer is running
A trigger toggling between running and stopped; while stopped the gates are closed and clock ticks are ignored
Returns the playhead to the beginning, or to the start repeat marker with that option set on the menu
Starts and stops playback
Starts and stops recording of the voltage arriving at the record inputs into the armed channels
Clears every segment out of the armed channels
Records the voltage arriving here into the armed channel; a polyphonic cable arms every channel it carries and records them all at once
With a cable patched here, recording happens only while this gate is open; with nothing patched, recording runs continuously and starts when the incoming voltage changes
Sets the velocity of each recorded note
A trigger clearing the armed channel; a polyphonic cable clears only the channels whose triggers fire
Arms one channel for recording; a click on a channel in the editor arms it, and mapped to a MIDI knob or a CV mapper the full sweep spans the channel list
The voltage of each channel at the playhead, one polyphonic channel per sequencer channel, over a range of -10V to 10V
A gate held open for the length of each segment, one polyphonic channel per sequencer channel
The velocity of each segment, one polyphonic channel per sequencer channel
A trigger each time the playhead reaches the end of the phrase
Note — the large display draws the phrase with the playhead as a vertical line, and clicking it opens an editor where CV segments are drawn and shaped as plain, S-curved or J-curved lines
Note — the small display names the phrase now playing, and clicking it lists the 25 phrases to choose from
Note — a MIDI file can be imported from the editor or dragged onto it from disk, and the sequence exported to a MIDI file from there
Note — a swing pattern set in the editor offsets quarter, eighth or sixteenth notes forwards or backwards by a chosen fraction, and a pattern set on a narrower part overrides a broader one
Note — quantisation set in the editor fixes how often a new segment is written while recording, so two steps per beat at 120BPM writes one every quarter of a second

Menu — Stop recording at end of song ends recording when the playhead reaches the end, without a second press of Record
Menu — Automatically add repeat markers when recording drops a start marker where recording began and an end marker where it stopped, and the playhead then loops that section
Menu — Light theme and Dark theme choose the panel colours
Menu — Save patch to use the free Entrian Player writes a copy of the patch with every Entrian sequencer replaced by its play-only counterpart from the Entrian Free plugin
CV.notes: The Reset and Run output jacks are not described in the manual, on the panel or in the binary, so they are left untagged.

lines: DAW-style timeline sequencer: up to 25 named songs, each ten tracks of clips holding pitched notes, drum notes or CV segments
The clock that drives playback, at four ticks per beat, which a clock module calls x4 or 1/16th
Chooses which of the 25 songs plays, C3 selecting the first and the 25 semitones up to C5 the last; set to trigger on the menu it steps to the next non-empty song or picks one at random
A trigger returning the playhead to the beginning, or to the start repeat marker with that option set on the menu; playback carries on immediately if the sequencer is running
A trigger toggling between running and stopped; while stopped the gates are closed and clock ticks are ignored
Returns the playhead to the beginning, or to the start repeat marker with that option set on the menu
Starts and stops playback
Starts and stops recording of the notes arriving at the record inputs into the armed clip
Clears every note out of the armed clip
Records into the armed clip: note pitches as 1V/oct for a melody clip, the incoming voltage for a CV clip, and note pitches choosing the voice for a drum clip
Records drum notes from a General MIDI drum kit, whose standard kit notes are mapped onto the ten voices
The note-on gate for recording, taken from the gate output of a MIDI-CV module
Sets the velocity of each recorded note
Arms one of the ten tracks for recording; a click on a track name arms it, and mapped to a MIDI knob or a CV mapper the full sweep spans the track list, one end to the other
Carries 1V/oct pitch where that track holds a melody clip, the segment voltage where it holds a CV clip, and a trigger where it holds a drum clip
A gate held open for the length of each note on that track, or a trigger on each accented note where the track holds a drum clip
The velocity of the note being played on that track
Note — the large display draws the song with the playhead as a vertical line, and clicking it opens a resizable editor where clips are added, moved, resized, aliased and filled with notes
Note — the small display names the song now playing, and clicking it lists the 25 songs to choose from
Note — a MIDI file can be imported from the editor or dragged onto it from disk, and the sequence exported to a MIDI file from there
Note — a swing pattern set in the editor offsets quarter, eighth or sixteenth notes by a chosen fraction, and can be set for the whole sequence, one song, one track, one clip or one channel
Note — an Alias clip plays the clip to its left without holding a copy of its notes, which is how a pattern is repeated along a track
Menu — Song selection input reads the song input as a pitch from C3 to C5, as a trigger stepping to the next non-empty song, or as a trigger picking a random song
Menu — Shared playhead links this module to other Entrian sequencers, one marked leader and the rest followers, so that all their playheads move together
Menu — Delay Clock/Reset/Run inputs adds a delay of a whole number of samples to those three inputs, to make up for the one-sample delay every cable in Rack adds; Auto is the default
Menu — Set playhead to start marker on reset sends a reset to the start repeat marker instead of to the beginning
Menu — Stop recording at end of song ends recording when the playhead reaches the end, without a second press of Record
Menu — Automatically add repeat markers when recording drops a start marker where recording began and an end marker where it stopped, and the playhead then loops that section
Menu — Light theme and Dark theme choose the panel colours
Menu — Save patch to use the free Entrian Player writes a copy of the patch with every Entrian sequencer replaced by its play-only counterpart from the Entrian Free plugin
Timeline.notes: The first output column carries a pitch, a voltage or a trigger depending on the kind of clip on that track, so it is given no family. The same goes for the combined pitch, CV and voice record input. The Reset and Run output jacks, and the End of clip output, are not described in the manual, on the panel or in the binary, so they are left untagged.
